correctness.rationale: The formal integral substitution y=e^t−1 gives G(y)=Σ g_k y^k with g0..3=(1,1,2,7); Stirling expansion yields a(n)=Σ g_k k! S(n,k). Mod 2^e, factorial divisibility truncates this to a finite sum Σ c_j j^n. Odd j are Carmichael-periodic; even j^n vanish by n≥e, proving period L_e from onset e. At n=e−1 only j≡2(mod4) contribute to the Carmichael-shift discrepancy; finite binomial inversion and mod-2 fourth-difference show their coefficient sum ≡g2+g3≡1, giving exact 2^(e−1). If some earlier tail had arbitrary period Q, its least period on the tail beginning e divides both Q and L_e; this forces equality at the obstructed n=e−1, contradiction. A separate e=1 parity check gives s1=0. Independent Stirling/arithmetic checks confirmed e=2..12; universality is proved by the finite-spectrum parity argument.
